title: Kasturba and Gandhi: The Saltless Vow of Love
summary: When Kasturba challenged whether he could give up salt and pulses himself, Gandhi immediately took a vow to abstain for a whole year, demonstrating that leadership begins at home.
keywords: Kasturba and Gandhi: The Saltless Vow of Love
full_text:
Behind the global titan of non-violence stood Kasturba Gandhi—a woman of indomitable will who never hesitated to hold her husband accountable.

In the ashram, Kasturba fell ill with chronic hemorrhage. Physicians advised that eliminating salt and pulses from her diet for several months was essential for recovery.

Kasturba resisted: "Food without salt is completely unpalatable! It is easy for doctors to prescribe impossible diets, but human beings cannot live without salt!"

Gandhi reasoned gently: "Ba, when a physician prescribes a cure for your health, you must demonstrate the discipline to follow it."

Kasturba snapped with frustration:
"You are always lecturing me! It is very easy to preach to others! Could you yourself give up salt and pulses for a whole year? I challenge you!"

Gandhi fell silent. A gentle smile touched his lips.

Looking into his wife's eyes, Gandhi answered with solemn warmth:
"Ba, your challenge is just. A teacher who does not practice what he preaches is an imposter.
Here and now, I make a vow:
**From this very day, for one full year, I shall not touch a grain of salt or a single pulse in my food!**
Whether you follow the diet or not, I shall honor my word!"

Kasturba was horrified: "Bapu! I spoke in anger! Please do not torment yourself over my hasty words!"

Gandhi refused to waver. For three hundred and sixty-five days, he consumed purely boiled, unseasoned vegetables without a trace of salt.

Moved by his supreme devotion, Kasturba willingly embraced the salt-free diet and recovered her health.

Gandhi proved that true moral leadership is forged not through authoritarian commands, but through voluntary personal sacrifice.
moral: True moral authority is never imposed by force; it is won when we hold ourselves to higher standards than we ask of others.
witty_quote: Before preaching discipline to others, a satyagrahi must first demonstrate it through his own personal sacrifice!
